# Delta Spec: issue-545 — Closing Reference Coverage

## Purpose

Govern on the FULL set of issues a merge will close, sourced from the platform where
the platform acts (the default branch), with regex resolution retained only where the
platform will not act (non-default/slice targets). Closes the measured under-coverage
defect (7/100 PRs) without reopening the ticket's stated defect (0/100, latent) or
false-blocking the 10/100 legitimate multi-target PRs.

---

## Domain: governance

### MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: REQ-S2-1 issue-link Job Gate — Verify Every Closing Target

The `issue-link` gate MUST resolve the FULL set of issues the merge will close. On a PR/MR
targeting the repository's default branch, the set MUST be sourced from the platform's
closing-references read (`closingIssueRefs`, `vcs-closing-refs-contract`) — the platform
only acts on closing keywords there. On a non-default (slice) target, where the platform
will not act on closing keywords at all (the #502/#503/#504 mirror case), the gate MUST
fall back to the existing regex-derived resolution (`extractIssueNumber`/`CLOSING_RE`/
`CHAIN_RE`), unchanged.

For every issue number in the resolved set, the gate MUST verify the `status:approved`
label. It MUST FAIL on the first unapproved target — a single unapproved issue in the set
fails the whole gate even when other targets are approved. It MUST PASS only when every
resolved target is approved.

When the platform closing-references read is uncomputable (unsupported CLI/API version,
network failure, rate limit, auth failure), the gate MUST fail closed with
`uncomputable: true` and a reason naming the cause. It MUST NOT silently degrade to a
smaller resolved set (regex-only, first-match) and report a false pass.

(Previously: resolved a single referenced issue via regex extraction — first
`CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE` match only — and verified only that one issue's approval label.)

#### Scenario: Missing issue reference fails

- GIVEN a PR body with no `Closes|Fixes|Resolves #N` pattern and no platform-reported closing issue
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it exits non-zero

#### Scenario: Single approved target passes

- GIVEN a default-branch PR closes exactly one issue and it carries `status:approved`
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it exits zero

#### Scenario: PR #592 regression — one approved, one not, FAILS

- GIVEN a default-branch PR's platform closing set is `[#477, #591]`; #477 carries `status:approved`, #591 does not
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it exits non-zero, citing #591 as unapproved

#### Scenario: Legitimate multi-target PR, all approved, PASSES

- GIVEN a default-branch PR's platform closing set has 2+ issues, every one carrying `status:approved`
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it exits zero (verified: 10/100 of the last merged PRs match this shape and must not be blocked)

#### Scenario: Non-default target — mirror case stays regex-resolved

- GIVEN a slice PR (base != default branch) whose body carries `Part of #473`, where the platform's own closing set for this MR is empty by design
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it resolves #473 via regex, not the platform read, and governs unchanged (over-governing, not under)

#### Scenario: Platform read uncomputable fails closed, never silently regex-only

- GIVEN a default-branch PR where the platform closing-references read cannot be performed (e.g. the installed CLI/API version does not expose the field)
- WHEN `issue-link` runs
- THEN it returns `{ pass: false, uncomputable: true, reason }` naming the cause — it never falls back to a regex-derived subset and reports pass

---

## Domain: governance-v3

### MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: REQ-L3-4 memory-gate Is Issue-Scoped (T2.1) — Multi-Target Permissive OR

REQ-L3-1's `memory-gate` job MUST NOT stop at a global existence check once at least one
issue in the current change's closing-reference set is detectable. `run-check.mjs` MUST
resolve the SAME closing-reference set `issue-link` resolves (platform-sourced on a
default-branch target, regex fallback on non-default), then filter `.memory/records/`
observations against that set with **permissive OR**: coverage is satisfied when ANY
issue in the set has a matching record. The gate MUST:

- FAIL when NO record in `.memory/records/` is scoped to ANY issue in the set (memory
  cache MISSING for the whole set).
- PASS with a WARN-flavored reason (non-blocking) when at least one issue in the set has
  scoped records but none is a `session_summary` (PARTIAL coverage).
- PASS cleanly when at least one issue in the set has a scoped `session_summary` (HIT) —
  even if other issues in the set have zero records.
- FALL BACK to the pre-existing global `memoryPresence()` check when no issue number can
  be resolved from `ctx` at all.

Tightening this to require a record per-issue (rather than any-of) is explicitly OUT OF
SCOPE of this change — it is a separate, stricter policy decision not made here.

(Previously: resolved and matched against a single issue number only.)

#### Scenario: Single-issue PR with a scoped session_summary passes cleanly

- GIVEN the resolved set is `{N}` and `.memory/records/` has a `session_summary` scoped to N
- WHEN `memory-gate` runs
- THEN it passes cleanly

#### Scenario: No record scoped to any target in the set fails

- GIVEN the resolved set is `{N, M}` and no record has `issue` in `{N, M}`
- WHEN `memory-gate` runs
- THEN it fails, citing the full set

#### Scenario: Multi-target PR — OR match on one of two targets passes

- GIVEN the resolved set is `{N, M}` and `.memory/records/` has a `session_summary` scoped to M only
- WHEN `memory-gate` runs
- THEN it passes cleanly (permissive OR — N need not have any record)

#### Scenario: No issue detectable — fallback to the global check, unchanged

- GIVEN `ctx.body` is absent or carries no detectable closing/Part-of reference
- WHEN `memory-gate` runs
- THEN it degrades to the pre-T2.1 global `memoryPresence()` check

---

## Domain: vcs-closing-refs-contract (NEW)

## Purpose

Cross-provider contract for reading which issues a merge will close according to the
platform itself (GitHub `closingIssuesReferences`, GitLab `closes_issues`) — distinct
from brain's regex-derived resolution. Consumed by `issue-link`/`memory-gate` (this same
change) only when the PR/MR targets the default branch.

### Requirement: REQ-VCR-1 closingIssueRefs Verb, Normalized Shape

Both `github.mjs` and `gitlab.mjs` MUST export a `closingIssueRefs({ project, number })`
verb returning `{ issues: number[] }` on success or `{ issues: null, uncomputable: true,
reason: string }` on failure. `issues` MUST be a plain array of issue numbers.

#### Scenario: Platform reports a closing set

- GIVEN a merged/open PR whose body the platform recognizes closing keywords in
- WHEN `closingIssueRefs` is called
- THEN `issues` matches the platform's own closing set, as plain numbers

#### Scenario: Zero closing refs is a valid empty array, not uncomputable

- GIVEN the platform recognizes no closing keyword for this PR
- WHEN `closingIssueRefs` is called
- THEN it returns `{ issues: [] }` — a successfully computed empty result, distinct from failure

### Requirement: REQ-VCR-2 Uncomputable Is Distinct From Empty, Always

The verb MUST NOT collapse a failed read into an empty array, regardless of failure
cause (unsupported CLI/API field or version, network failure, rate limit, auth failure).
Any such failure MUST return `{ issues: null, uncomputable: true, reason }` naming the
cause, and MUST NOT throw to the caller.

#### Scenario: Read cannot be performed on the running environment

- GIVEN the runtime cannot answer this read (e.g. the installed CLI/API surface lacks the needed field)
- WHEN `closingIssueRefs` is called
- THEN it returns `{ issues: null, uncomputable: true, reason }`, never `{ issues: [] }`

#### Scenario: Transient failure normalizes the same way

- GIVEN the underlying call throws or rejects (network, rate limit, auth)
- WHEN `closingIssueRefs` is called
- THEN it returns the same uncomputable shape, never a thrown error

### Requirement: REQ-VCR-3 Verb Registered at All Three Drift-Guard Sources

`closingIssueRefs` MUST be added, in one commit, to: the `vcs-contract.md` Required
Verbs table; `cli.mjs`'s `VERBS` array; and both providers' exports.
`verb-contract-drift-guard.test.mjs` MUST pass with the verb present at all three.

#### Scenario: Registered together, drift-guard passes

- GIVEN the verb is added to `VERBS`, `vcs-contract.md`, and both providers in the same commit
- WHEN `verb-contract-drift-guard.test.mjs` runs
- THEN it passes

#### Scenario: Partial registration is caught

- GIVEN both providers export the verb but `VERBS` or the doc table omits it
- WHEN `verb-contract-drift-guard.test.mjs` runs
- THEN it fails, naming the missing source

---

## Explicitly Out of Scope

- `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE` vocabulary or default-branch conditionality — unchanged.
- `actor-check.mjs` and `brain-metrics.mjs`'s own copies of issue extraction — follow-up.
- Retroactive remediation of issue #591 — maintainer decision, not enforced here.
- Tightening `memory-gate` to one record per issue — separate policy change.
